title: Policy cascade shadowing allows transient quota overage during regional failover
creator: Amina Rodriguez
description: During a simulated regional failover test we observed that several enterprise customers were briefly able to exceed per-org quotas for specific routes. The enforcement path accepted requests for ~60s beyond the quota without emitting alerts, charging, or throttling. This ticket tracks investigation, a short-term mitigation for live traffic, and a permanent fix in the policy evaluation + enforcement pipeline.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure org O123 with per-org limit 1,000 req/min and a stricter per-route limit 100 req/min for /generate in region us-west.
2) Create a route alias mapping (route alias R-A -> /generate) used by gateway during failover.
3) Simulate edge failover: mark us-west primary unhealthy; promote us-east and apply alias mapping.
4) Send synthetic traffic from multiple clients targeting org O123 across route alias R-A and observe enforcement decisions on edge nodes.
5) Observe that per-route counters are enforced but per-org bucket does not decrement for ~60 seconds; throttles do not trigger and billing meters show missing debits.
observed_behavior: Per-route debits recorded locally on edge (per-route counters increment) but per-org aggregate debit messages are either dropped or applied to a stale policy version. Enforcement returned HTTP 200 for requests that should have been throttled; billing pipeline shows undercount for the same interval. No error logs were emitted in the fast path because the evaluation returned a permissive decision from the edge cache.
expected_behavior: Per-route and per-org quotas should be evaluated atomically (or with a well-defined ordering) such that no request is permitted when it would exceed either the route or org quota. Enforcement decisions must decrement meters consistently and emit quota-exceeded metrics and alerts.
investigation_notes: - Initial trace of request path shows evaluation order: fast path checks route-level quota -> allows -> asynchronously emits org-debit event to aggregator.

- Edge policy cache had TTL 70s; control-plane policy rollout set new policy version with window_seconds truncated during serialization so the org-level sliding window was treated as 3600 instead of 60 in some nodes.

- There is an observable race when alias resolution happens: edge resolves alias to a runtime route ID and looks up policy by route-id, but org-level policy lookup uses a cached policy-key that lags during failover causing a permissive fallback.
- A bug in the per-org debit path: failed retries to the central meter-aggregator are silently suppressed by a newly-introduced backoff layer, causing debit messages to be dropped instead of queued.
- Reproduced in staging: enabling verbose policy-cache logging shows entries with mismatched policy_version on edges handling the same request, confirming cache staleness.
- No CPU or memory pressure; this looks like a correctness/regression issue in policy serialization + cache coherence rather than an infra capacity problem.
root_cause: Multiple contributing issues: (1) policy serialization regression truncated numeric window fields when modelled as 32-bit ints, leading to inconsistent effective windows across nodes; (2) edge policy cache TTL (70s) exceeded the expected control-plane publish cadence during failover, allowing stale permissive policies to be used; (3) the async org-debit path introduced a suppression/backoff change that can drop debit messages under certain error returns, resulting in undercounting and no immediate throttle feedback.
mitigations: Short-term (hotfix): Pin policy cache TTL to 5s on all edge pools in affected regions via emergency config flag to reduce stale decisions during rollouts and failovers.

Short-term (hotfix): Deploy a reactive guard in the enforcement path that performs a synchronous org-bucket read-before-allow for requests that match enterprise orgs (top 20% of traffic) until the permanent fix is deployed.
Medium-term: Revert the suppression change in the debit retry/backoff logic so debit messages are queued and retried persistently for 30s before failing, and add an explicit dead-letter queue metric.

Long-term: Fix policy serialization to preserve 64-bit numeric fields, add deterministic policy-version stamping, and implement a distributed policy invalidation handshake between control plane and edge nodes to guarantee cache coherence during failovers.
Operational: Create an alert that triggers when per-route successful requests exceed per-org debits by more than 5% for 30s.
Customer ops: Notify affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps; offer credits if bill undercounting caused downstream surprises.
proposed_solution_steps: 1) Emergency config: roll edge config to TTL=5s for policy cache (ops runbook step).
2) Implement synchronous org-bucket guard for enterprise orgs in enforcement fast path and ship behind a feature flag.
3) Fix serialization: audit all policy proto/json conversion paths and add unit tests for numeric field preservation and policy_version monotonicity.
4) Rework debit pipeline: ensure retries persist across transient errors and add DLQ metrics; add end-to-end tests that assert eventual debit delivery under simulated aggregator failures.
5) Add integration tests that simulate alias-based failover and assert per-route+per-org invariants at high QPS.
6) Postmortem + documentation: update runbooks and add a checklist for policy rollouts that includes cache TTL coordination and feature-flag windows.
7) Schedule a canary rollout and extended validation (72h) before global rollout.
8) Post-deploy: monitor new alert and runbook metrics and verify recovery behavior in a follow-up chaos experiment.
acceptance_criteria: - Edges no longer use stale policy versions during failover when runbook steps are executed (test harness simulating failover passes).
- Debit messages reach aggregator within 10s under normal network conditions and queued reliably under transient errors (integration test).
- No silent permissive decisions observed for enterprise orgs in chaos failover test (assert 0 permissive anomalies in 1M requests run).
- New alerts fire correctly when per-route successes diverge from per-org debits beyond threshold.
- PRs merged: serialization fix, debit retry revert, edge TTL config and synchronous guard feature flag.
notes: - Engineering lead (SRE): coordinate TTL change during low-traffic window.
- PM: prepare customer communication drafts for affected enterprise customers.
- Security review: not required for hotfix, but serialization change must be reviewed before GA (security_review_required=true).
